input.requirements_spec: Enable creators to discover active campaigns in a marketplace, check their eligibility, and submit applications. Enable brands to view, rank, and accept or reject applications. Key requirements: (1) Campaign marketplace with filters (category, fee range, deadline) and relevance sorting. (2) Per-criterion eligibility check (follower count, engagement rate, content category, region). (3) Application submission with content outline, estimated delivery date, and requested fee. (4) Fit-score ranking for brands reviewing applications (weighted: category 40%, follower 20%, engagement 20%, history 10%, fee competitiveness 10%). (5) Budget reservation on acceptance using pessimistic locking to prevent race conditions. (6) Application state machine: submitted → accepted/rejected/withdrawn. (7) Unique constraint: one active application per creator per campaign.
input.system_context: Existing xhs-campaign-service (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy async). Established patterns: Repository for data access, Service for business logic, Pydantic schemas for request/response, custom exceptions (NotFoundError, ConflictError, ForbiddenError). Auth via X-User-Id header → CurrentUser dependency. User model exists with: id (UUID str), username, email, display_name, role (creator/brand/admin), follower_count, bio. Campaign model is assumed to exist (from C2-01) with: id, brand_id FK, title, description, status enum, total_budget (Decimal), remaining_budget (Decimal), min_fee, max_fee, application_deadline, content_deadline, publish_deadline, eligibility criteria fields (min_follower_count, min_engagement_rate, required_categories JSON, region_restrictions JSON). Tech stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery.
input.constraints: Performance: marketplace listing < 300ms p95 for 5K campaigns. Concurrency: budget reservation must use SELECT FOR UPDATE. Security: creators see only own applications, brands see only their campaign applications, fit score weights not exposed. Data integrity: budget operations must be transactional.

tables.model_code_sketch:
class Application(Base, TimestampMixin, SoftDeleteMixin):
    __tablename__ = 'applications'

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True, default=generate_uuid)
    campaign_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), ForeignKey('campaigns.id'), nullable=False)
    creator_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[ApplicationStatus] = mapped_column(nullable=False, default=ApplicationStatus.SUBMITTED)
    content_outline: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(1000), nullable=False)
    estimated_delivery_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(Date, nullable=False)
    requested_fee: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(Numeric(12, 2), nullable=False)
    fit_score: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=True)
    rejection_reason: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(500), nullable=True)
    responded_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
    version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=1)

integration_points.interaction: Read campaign details (eligibility criteria, budget, deadlines, status). On accept: lock campaign row (SELECT FOR UPDATE), deduct requested_fee from remaining_budget, flush.
integration_points.interface: Direct repository access via CampaignRepository within the same DB transaction
integration_points.failure_handling: If campaign not found or not active, raise NotFoundError/ValidationError before any state change

integration_points.interaction: Read creator profile (follower_count, engagement_rate, content_categories, region) for eligibility check and fit score calculation.
integration_points.interface: Direct repository access via UserRepository within the same DB session
integration_points.failure_handling: If user not found, raise NotFoundError (should not happen as user is authenticated)

integration_points.interaction: Send notifications on: application submitted (to brand), application accepted/rejected (to creator), application withdrawn (to brand).
integration_points.interface: Async Celery task: send_notification.delay(user_id, notification_type, payload)
integration_points.failure_handling: Fire-and-forget via Celery. Notification failure must not block the application operation. Log errors for monitoring.

technical_decisions.decision: Use pessimistic locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE) for budget reservation on acceptance
alternatives_considered: Optimistic locking with version check on campaign row — rejected because under high concurrency, retries add latency and complexity
Application-level mutex via Redis SETNX — rejected because it doesn't guarantee DB consistency if the app crashes between lock and commit
technical_decisions.justification: SELECT FOR UPDATE within a single DB transaction is the simplest correct solution. The lock scope is narrow (one campaign row), contention is low (acceptance is a low-frequency operation per campaign), and PostgreSQL handles deadlock detection natively.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Slightly higher latency on concurrent acceptances for the same campaign (serialized), but correctness is non-negotiable for financial operations.

technical_decisions.decision: Compute fit_score at application submission time and store it, not compute on-read
alternatives_considered: Compute on every list request — rejected because score calculation requires joining creator profile data, which adds query complexity and latency on a frequently-accessed brand endpoint
technical_decisions.justification: Fit score depends on creator profile at application time (which we've decided is the evaluation snapshot). Pre-computing and storing allows simple ORDER BY fit_score DESC queries. Stored score can be re-computed in bulk if weights change.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Stored scores become stale if creator profile changes, but per requirement EC-2.4, eligibility is snapshot-at-application-time.

technical_decisions.decision: Evaluate eligibility at query time (not cached) for the eligibility check endpoint, but snapshot at application time
alternatives_considered: Cache eligibility in Redis for 5 minutes — considered but deferred to P2 since eligibility check is a simple in-memory comparison once the campaign and user data are loaded
technical_decisions.justification: Eligibility check is a lightweight comparison of user fields against campaign criteria — no external API calls. Two DB reads (user + campaign) are sufficient. Caching adds complexity for marginal gain at current scale.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Each eligibility check hits the DB. If marketplace browsing loads increase, add Redis caching as a P2 optimization.

technical_decisions.decision: Use Decimal(12,2) for monetary fields (requested_fee), not Float
alternatives_considered: Float — rejected due to floating-point precision errors in financial calculations
technical_decisions.justification: Monetary values must be exact. Decimal(12,2) supports values up to 9,999,999,999.99 which is well beyond campaign budget ranges. Matches the campaign model's budget field type.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Decimal operations are slightly slower than float, negligible at this scale.

technical_decisions.decision: Partial unique index for one-active-application-per-creator constraint instead of application-level check
alternatives_considered: Check-then-insert in application code — rejected because it is vulnerable to race conditions between the check and insert
technical_decisions.justification: A partial unique index WHERE status NOT IN ('withdrawn') AND is_deleted = FALSE enforces the constraint at the database level, which is race-condition-proof. Creators who withdraw can re-apply because their withdrawn application is excluded from the index.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Partial unique indexes are PostgreSQL-specific (not portable to MySQL). Acceptable since PostgreSQL is our chosen database.

application_submission.title: Application Submission Flow
steps: 1. Creator calls POST /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/applications with ApplicationCreate body
2. API layer extracts CurrentUser (must be creator role)
6. Service loads Creator profile via UserRepository.get_by_id(creator.id)
7. EligibilityEngine.check(creator, campaign) → raises ForbiddenError if ineligible
8. Validate: requested_fee between campaign.min_fee and campaign.max_fee
12. ApplicationRepository.create(application) — DB unique constraint handles duplicate check
error_paths: Step 5: campaign not active or deadline passed → 422 ValidationError
Step 7: creator ineligible → 403 ForbiddenError with per-criterion details
Step 8-9: fee or date out of range → 422 ValidationError
Step 12: unique constraint violation → 409 ConflictError 'Already applied'

acceptance_with_budget_lock.title: Application Acceptance with Budget Reservation (Race Condition Handling)
steps: 2. API layer extracts CurrentUser (must be brand role)
4. Load Application via repo — validate status == 'submitted'
5. Load Campaign — validate brand_user.id == campaign.brand_id (ownership check)
7. BEGIN TRANSACTION (already in DB session context)
8. CampaignRepository.get_by_id_for_update(campaign_id) — executes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on campaigns row → acquires row-level exclusive lock
10. If insufficient: raise ConflictError('Insufficient campaign budget'). Lock released on rollback.
14. Flush both changes in same transaction
acceptance_with_budget_lock.concurrency_note: If two concurrent accept requests target the same campaign: Request A acquires the row lock at step 8. Request B blocks at step 8 until A commits or rolls back. After A commits, B sees the updated remaining_budget and may fail at step 9 if budget is now insufficient. This guarantees budget is never over-allocated.

fit_score_algorithm.formula: fit_score = category_match × 0.4 + follower_score × 0.2 + engagement_score × 0.2 + history_score × 0.1 + fee_competitiveness × 0.1

components.name: category_match
components.calculation: len(intersection(creator.categories, campaign.required_categories)) / len(campaign.required_categories). If campaign has no required categories, default 1.0.

components.name: follower_score
components.calculation: min(creator.follower_count / campaign.min_follower_count, 1.0) if min_follower_count > 0 else 1.0. Guards: if creator.follower_count == 0, score = 0.0.

components.name: history_score
components.calculation: For v1, all creators get a neutral 0.5 (no historical campaign data yet). Future: completed_campaigns / total_accepted_campaigns.

components.name: fee_competitiveness
components.calculation: 1.0 - ((requested_fee - campaign.min_fee) / (campaign.max_fee - campaign.min_fee)). Lower fee = higher score. If min_fee == max_fee, default 1.0.

fit_score_algorithm.output_range: 0.0 – 1.0 (stored as Float, displayed as percentage to brand)
fit_score_algorithm.config_location: Weights defined as constants in eligibility_engine.py. Configurable via environment variables for tuning without code changes.
